concerns.text: FR-010 mandates min-max normalization of FQY but never states the scaling statistics are computed on the TRAINING set only. If min/max are fit on the pooled dataset, test-set target information leaks into preprocessing — undermining the scaffold-disjoint validation the whole design rests on (Constitution VI). Specify train-fit-only scaling.

FR-012 skips any molecule with atom/bond types unseen in training. Applied at evaluation time this selectively drops test molecules based on training-set content, biasing the reported R²/RMSE/MAE (the test set is no longer the scaffold-split sample). Skipping should apply at inference on new inputs, not to held-out evaluation molecules; at minimum require logging and reporting of dropped test fraction.

The interpretability validation hinges on a 'curated reference set of fluorophore motifs (Supplementary Table S1)' whose provenance, construction rule, and independence from the model's training data are entirely unspecified. If the motif list is assembled post hoc from the same chemistry the attributions highlight, the ≥60% overlap check becomes near-tautological. Define the source/selection rule for Table S1 and its independence from the attribution pipeline.

FR-015 records solvent/temperature/method metadata but no FR uses it. FQY is strongly condition-dependent; pooling measurements across solvents/temperatures adds target noise the spec should at least acknowledge (e.g., report condition heterogeneity or restrict to a dominant condition) — otherwise the metadata requirement is scientifically inert.
